settings.title: I Found Mycotoxins Where No One Was Looking
settings.founder_credentials: Susan Gonya, MS, RD, Pediatric Nutrition Researcher
settings.custom_content:
My name is Susan Gonya. I’m a dietitian, a nurse, a researcher, and a mother. I am also the founder of Clean Food Solutions. My work began with a simple question. What are we really feeding our children?

What I uncovered was far more serious than I ever imagined. Mycotoxins, which are toxic compounds produced by mold, are showing up in everyday foods like bread, cereal, oats, and even human milk. These invisible contaminants are linked to gut inflammation, immune dysfunction, and developmental issues in children. Yet they often go unnoticed and unregulated.

Clean Food Solutions was founded in response to these findings. It is a small, women-owned company committed to uncovering the truth, sharing scientific knowledge, and helping families make informed choices to protect their health.

settings.text: Our approach highlights mycotoxins present in daily foods and provides guidance for making safer, healthier choices.
Our recipes are rooted in science, driven by love, and focused on change. New recipes will be posted regularly to help guide your journey toward cleaner living.

settings.title: We identified where mold contaminants can most likely be found in foods through peer-reviewed research and then utilized rigorous laboratory testing.

settings.description: Microbiome Labs leads in microbiome science with rigorously tested formulas that support gut and immune health. Peer-reviewed studies and discounts are available on the website for members. Our founder began working with Microbiome Labs many years ago when she discovered that many of the Bacillus probiotic cultures have antifungal properties and that some have been studied for their ability detoxify harmful trichothecene mycotoxins like DON. However, the research in this area is still young, and those who decide to use these products will be asked to check with their healthcare provider before starting a new probiotic.

Fatty15 is a science-first wellness company that produces C15:0, a pure, vegan-friendly fatty acid that has been shown to support cellular health and longevity. This is a first-of-its-kind saturated fatty acid supplement that was developed based on scientific research that began with dolphins, where supplementation demonstrated anti-inflammatory, metabolic, and longevity-related effects.

Born out of a passion for clean, allergen-free ingredients, Relative Foods launched in 2019 with just two staples. Today, it offers over 25 organic and natural products. All their products are tested for gluten at a much stricter standard than is required by the FDA, so those with gluten intolerance, food allergies, and Celiac disease can feel comfortable purchasing these products. Their attention to food quality and safety is awe-inspiring, and their non-grain ingredients are among the cleanest we have ever tested for mycotoxins–truly a tribute to good manufacturing practices. We are proud to offer Relative Food products to you, and while we only offer tapioca flour, table sugar, and baking soda at this time, we plan to add products as we go.

Coffee can be moldy. Coffee beans are grown, harvested, processed, and packaged in sites that are sometimes far from their final destinations. They also undergo many steps in transportation and food processing. In addition, climate change, poor drying and storage conditions, insect damage, and infections present at harvest can all contribute to mold and mycotoxin contamination in coffee.

New England Cupboard is a specialty food mix manufacturer and distributor located in Hermon, Maine. New England Cupboard was founded in 1995. They have since acquired other smaller companies, including Winterport Co., Cook In The Kitchen, and the popular Bakewell Cream. New England Cupboard is currently owned and operated by Jim Collins, of Hampden, Maine.

Every spoonful unveils an exceptionally smooth texture, paired with a flavor that is both rich and tantalizingly deep. Beyond its luscious taste, this cacao powder stands as a beacon of purity, having been meticulously tested for mycotoxins, including aflatoxins, to ensure consumer safety. By eliminating the risk of hidden mold toxins, Addictive Wellness sets a new gold standard in cacao quality and purity.

360 Cookware combines cutting-edge technology with timeless craftsmanship to bring you cookware that outperforms and outlasts the competition. Our commitment to quality, health, and sustainability sets a new standard in the culinary world.

settings.main_text: In today's world of ultra-processed foods and chemical agriculture, our bodies face constant exposure to hidden toxins like mycotoxins and pesticide residues, which may be linked to the increasing rates of chronic illnesses.

settings.sub_text: Inspired by her son’s struggle with gastrointestinal illness, healthcare professional Susan Gonya shares her family's journey in *The Fungus Among Us*. She explores the hidden dangers of mycotoxins in processed foods, highlighting their impact on health. With a blend of personal stories and clinical insights, Gonya simplifies complex science, empowering readers to understand how mycotoxins affect gut health, immunity, and overall well-being.

settings.subtitle: Susan's book is filled with simple, wholesome recipes you can enjoy every day.
settings.research_description: Informative, inspiring, and packed with over 100 practical, easy-to-follow recipes, The Fungus Among Us gives you the tools to reduce your toxic load and reclaim your health—one bite at a time.

settings.title: Challenging the Norm
settings.description: While completing her graduate work, Susan begins noticing alarming gaps in public knowledge about food contaminants, especially in children's diets.

settings.title: Mycotoxins Discovery
settings.description: Through early literature reviews, Susan identifies Deoxynivalenol (DON) as a common yet underreported contaminant in grains. This sparks her first deep-dive into the science.

settings.title: Toxins & Inflammation
settings.description: Her analysis of DON and similar mycotoxins reveals strong associations with gut inflammation, immune disruption, and developmental issues in children.

settings.title: Solving Systemic Gaps
settings.description: She noted that many mycotoxins, while prevalent in the food supply, are not only understudied but remain unregulated or poorly regulated. Consequently, contaminated products appeared to be finding their way into our homes and diets. She began searching for mycotoxin-free ingredients to make food for her family, testing them using mycotoxin screening equipment and collaborating with a laboratory that could verify her results through advanced laboratory techniques.

settings.title: Publication & Peer Review
settings.description: Susan began to share the results of her work at conferences through poster presentations. Over time, her research began to gain traction in academic circles, leading to peer-reviewed publications and collaborations within the scientific community.

settings.title: Building the Solution
settings.description: Frustrated by inaction, Susan began testing foods from various food producers, looking for basic ingredients produced using stricter cleanliness and quality assurance practices. As suspected, food manufacturers with better quality control practices also seemed to be producing products that were free from mold contaminants.  Companies that utilized cold storage, strict cleaning protocols, and dehumidification were producing the cleanest ingredients. Fresh whole foods and foods produced by companies addressing food allergies with strict quality procedures appeared to be among the cleanest. With this information, she began bridging the gap between research and what made its way to her family’s table.

settings.title: Expanding Health
settings.description: She developed partnerships with companies dedicated to producing higher-quality foods for consumers and founded Clean Food Solutions. From public speaking to brand advocacy, Susan works to make science accessible and empower families with tools like her book The Fungus Among Us: Science and Recipes for a Cleaner Diet to avoid harmful mycotoxin exposures.
